title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Employees
tiers.description: All Pacific Current Directors, officers, employees and contractors globally. Subject only to the general insider trading prohibition and confidentiality duty (sections 4.1-4.2); the additional Blackout Period, clearance, hedging and short-term trading restrictions in section 4.3 apply only if also a Restricted Person.

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: All Directors, all executive direct reports to the Board and/or an Executive Director (Senior Executives), other employees/contractors identified due to their position (Senior Leaders, committee members), Associates of Restricted Persons, and other persons identified by the Board. Subject to Blackout Periods, prior clearance and notification, post-trade reporting, no hedging/derivatives, margin lending clearance, and discouragement of short-term/speculative trading.

tiers.name: Chair of the Pacific Current Board
tiers.description: Board Chair; distinguished only for clearance, approved by the Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee.

tiers.name: Other Pacific Current Directors
tiers.description: Directors other than the Chair; distinguished only for clearance, approved by the Chair of the Board.

tiers.name: Senior Executives, Senior Leaders and other Restricted Persons
tiers.description: Senior Executives, Senior Leaders and other persons identified as Restricted Persons; distinguished only for clearance, approved by the Chair of the Audit & Risk Committee or the Company Secretary.

tiers.name: Associates of Restricted Persons
tiers.description: Spouse or partner, dependent children, trustees of a trust under which the person/spouse/children may benefit, companies in which the person holds a majority or otherwise controls, and other entities where the person is a director, secretary or executive officer. Treated as Restricted Persons for the additional restrictions.

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may specify any other Blackout Period from time to time (4.3.3(b)(v)). Pacific Current may also impose an ad-hoc Blackout Period, for example where it relies on a Listing Rule disclosure exception; Restricted Persons are simply notified a Blackout Period is in place and must not trade, whether or not personally aware of inside information. The policy does not separately address whether the reason for an ad-hoc blackout is kept confidential.

rules.detail: Absolute, unconditional ban on dealing in derivatives related to Pacific Current Securities, expressly naming put and call options; applies regardless of vesting state and with no clearance or waiver route (the 4.3.10 waiver only covers the clearance/notification steps in 4.3.4/4.3.5, not this substantive prohibition).
rules.evidence: A Restricted Person must not engage in hedging arrangements, deal in derivatives or enter into other arrangements which vary economic risk related to Pacific Current Securities including, for example, dealing in warrants, equity swaps, put and call options, contracts for difference and other contracts intended to secure a profit or avoid a loss based on fluctuations in the price of Pacific Current Securities.

rules.detail: Blanket hedging ban expressly extended to unvested, holding-locked and scheme securities, with no carve-out for vested unrestricted holdings; same clause as derivatives.
rules.evidence: This prohibition includes engaging in hedging or other arrangements that would have the effect of limiting the economic risk in connection with Pacific Current Securities including Securities which are unvested, subject to a holding lock or issued pursuant to a Pacific Current equity-based remuneration scheme.

rules.detail: Monetisation instruments (e.g. prepaid variable forwards) are not named but fall within the broad catch-all barring 'other arrangements which vary economic risk' and contracts 'intended to secure a profit or avoid a loss based on fluctuations in the price' of Pacific Current Securities.
rules.evidence: enter into other arrangements which vary economic risk related to Pacific Current Securities ... and other contracts intended to secure a profit or avoid a loss based on fluctuations in the price of Pacific Current Securities.

rules.detail: Short selling is not named anywhere in the policy and there is no defined 'Dealing' concept to sweep it in by implication.
Securities lending is not mentioned anywhere in the policy.
Contracts for difference are expressly named as a prohibited example of a hedging/derivative arrangement.
rules.evidence: including, for example, dealing in warrants, equity swaps, put and call options, contracts for difference and other contracts intended to secure a profit or avoid a loss based on fluctuations in the price of Pacific Current Securities.

rules.detail: Margin loans over Restricted Persons' Pacific Current Securities holdings are expressly permitted subject to the ordinary prior clearance/notification process, with an accompanying obligation to maintain sufficient cash or collateral to meet margin calls.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons are permitted to take out margin loans over their holdings in Pacific Current Securities provided they first comply with the applicable clearance and notification process as set out in section 4.3.4.

rules.detail: Granting security is not separately named, but 'other secured financing arrangement' is contemplated alongside margin lending as something that can be 'previously approved in accordance with this policy', implying encumbrance is permitted if cleared.
rules.evidence: an involuntary disposal of securities that results from a margin lender or financier exercising its rights under a margin lending or other secured financing arrangement that has previously been approved in accordance with this policy.

rules.detail: Beyond margin loans, 'other secured financing arrangements' are expressly referenced as a category that can be cleared in advance; no blanket ban exists, unlike the hedging ban in 4.3.7.
rules.evidence: a margin lender or financier exercising its rights under a margin lending or other secured financing arrangement that has previously been approved in accordance with this policy.

rules.detail: Advisory ('should not') rather than an absolute 'must not' ban on short-term or speculative trading; no defined holding period, LIFO basis or carve-outs are specified.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons should not trade in Pacific Current Securities on a short-term basis or for speculative trading gain.

clearance.tier: Chair of the Pacific Current Board
clearance.approver: Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee
clearance.post_trade_to: Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee and the Company Secretary
clearance.post_trade_deadline: no fixed deadline stated for confirming the trade; Directors must give the Company Secretary sufficient ASX reporting information within 3 business days of the change
clearance.evidence: If granted to a Director, Senior Executive or Senior Leader, consent to trade is only valid for a period of five trading days after notification of approval, unless otherwise notified by the Authorising Officer to the Restricted Person. Trading consent is automatically deemed to be withdrawn if the person becomes aware of inside information prior to trading.

clearance.approver: Chair of the Pacific Current Board
clearance.post_trade_to: Chair of the Pacific Current Board and the Company Secretary
clearance.post_trade_deadline: no fixed deadline stated for confirming the trade; Directors must give the Company Secretary sufficient ASX reporting information within 3 business days of the change
clearance.evidence: Any approval to trade can be given, withdrawn or refused by Pacific Current in its discretion without giving any reasons. A decision to refuse approval is final and binding on the person seeking the approval.

clearance.tier: Senior Executives, Senior Leaders and other Restricted Persons
clearance.approver: Chair of the Pacific Current Audit & Risk Committee or the Company Secretary
clearance.post_trade_to: Authorising Officer and the Company Secretary
clearance.evidence: Once a Restricted Person has completed a trade in Pacific Current Securities, the Authorising Officer (if applicable) described in section 4.3.4 and in all cases, the Company Secretary, must be advised that the trade has been completed and attach the trade confirmation.

short_term.evidence: Restricted Persons should not trade in Pacific Current Securities on a short-term basis or for speculative trading gain.

exceptions.evidence: the additional restrictions in this policy do not prohibit Restricted Persons from transferring Securities where there is no change to the beneficial owner of the Securities.

the additional restrictions in this policy do not prohibit Restricted Persons from acquiring Securities or exercising an option or right under a Pacific Current employee incentive scheme subject to the terms of the relevant employee incentive scheme.
the additional restrictions in this policy do not prohibit Restricted Persons from acquiring Securities under a Pacific Current dividend reinvestment plan (if active).

exceptions.approver: Pacific Current Board (approves the plan/timing and structure of the offer)
exceptions.evidence: trading under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the security holders, such as a rights issue, a security plan purchase and an equal access buy-back, where the plan that determines the timing and structure of the offer has been approved by the Pacific Current Board.

an investment in, or trading in units of, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme only investing in Pacific Current Securities) where the assets of the fund or other scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party.

an involuntary disposal of securities that results from a margin lender or financier exercising its rights under a margin lending or other secured financing arrangement that has previously been approved in accordance with this policy.

exceptions.approver: Authorising Officer described in section 4.3.4 (or Company Secretary if none applies)
exceptions.evidence: Exceptional circumstances include severe financial hardship, compulsion by a court order or any other circumstances that are deemed exceptional by the person described in section 4.3.4.

exceptions.approver: Authorising Officer described in section 4.3.4 (or Company Secretary if none applies)
exceptions.evidence: compulsion by a court order or any other circumstances that are deemed exceptional by the person described in section 4.3.4.

financing_disclosure: Directors: at inception of a margin loan or other secured financing arrangement (treated as a Dealing requiring prior clearance under 4.3.4) - notify the Company Secretary within 3 business days of the change so ASX can be informed within 5 business days.

exemption_authority: Exceptional circumstances waiver under 4.3.10 (severe financial hardship, court order, or other circumstances the Authorising Officer/Company Secretary deems exceptional) excuses only the clearance and post-trade notification steps in 4.3.4/4.3.5, valid for five trading days; it does not excuse substantive prohibitions such as the 4.3.7 hedging/derivatives ban.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Restricted Person must not engage in hedging arrangements, deal in derivatives or enter into other arrangements which vary economic risk related to Pacific Current Securities including, for example, dealing in warrants, equity swaps, put and call options, contracts for difference and other contracts intended to secure a profit or avoid a loss based on fluctuations in the price of Pacific Current Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is a flat, unwaivable ban naming put and call options specifically, so the hedge legs of a collar cannot be entered into by any Director or Senior Executive regardless of vesting state or clearance.

bespoke_clauses.topic: waiver does not reach substantive bans
bespoke_clauses.clause: the Restricted Person must apply to the Authorising Officer described in section 4.3.4 for a waiver from compliance with the provisions in sections 4.3.4 or 4.3.5.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The only waiver mechanism excuses clearance/notification procedure, not the section 4.3.7 hedging ban itself, so financial hardship cannot be used to obtain a collar exemption.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons must ensure they have sufficient available cash or collateral to meet margin calls, including in periods of volatility.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even though the loan leg is permitted with clearance, the bank/borrower must maintain buffer collateral, which is a covenant point for structuring a secured facility.

bespoke_clauses.clause: an involuntary disposal of securities that results from a margin lender or financier exercising its rights under a margin lending or other secured financing arrangement that has previously been approved in accordance with this policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A lender's enforcement sale under a pre-approved secured facility is excluded from the Blackout Period ban, so the loan (if it existed without the banned hedge) could be enforced at any time without breaching the policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Trading consent is automatically deemed to be withdrawn if the person becomes aware of inside information prior to trading. ... If approval to trade Pacific Current Securities is refused, the person seeking the approval must keep that information confidential and not disclose it to anyone.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any cleared leg of a transaction (e.g. the loan) must complete within 5 trading days and lapses on inside information, and a refusal cannot be disclosed to the bank counterparty.

bespoke_clauses.clause: your associates include: your spouse or partner ... any trustee of a trust ... any company in which you hold (directly or indirectly) a majority of the shares or otherwise control.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing a collar or loan through a spouse, family trust or controlled company does not escape the section 4.3.7 hedging ban, since Associates of Restricted Persons are themselves Restricted Persons.

summary: A funded collar is not possible for any Pacific Current Director or Senior Executive because all such persons are Restricted Persons, and section 4.3.7 imposes a blanket, unconditional ban on hedging, dealing in derivatives, and other arrangements that vary economic risk related to Pacific Current Securities, expressly naming put and call options and contracts for difference, across all vesting states (unvested, holding-locked and unrestricted). There is no clearance, board discretion or exceptional-circumstances waiver that reaches this substantive prohibition; the 4.3.10 waiver only excuses the procedural clearance/notification steps in 4.3.4/4.3.5. The financing leg alone is permitted: Restricted Persons may take out margin loans, and by extension other secured financing arrangements, over their holdings with prior written clearance and notice to the Company Secretary, subject to maintaining sufficient collateral for margin calls, and a lender's enforcement sale under a pre-approved facility is excluded from the Blackout Period restriction. Because the hedge cannot lawfully be written, the bank could only offer an unhedged, clearance-based share-secured loan, not a true funded collar, and Associates (spouses, trusts, controlled companies) are equally bound so cannot be used to work around the ban.
